publicBrief.acceptedPolicy: A download must pass the owner-aware view_document check on the root document before serving any selected file version.
publicBrief.currentQuestion: At DocumentViewSet.download handler entry, can an authenticated user download a requested version document they own when its root document is owned by someone else and they lack an object view grant on that root? Assume the user has the required global view permission and the documents exist.
premises: At download entry, the authenticated caller has global document view permission and owns the requested version, but a different user owns the existing root document and the caller has no object view grant on that root.
requiredResponseDetails: Identify which object is checked and which file object would be served; do not collapse version ownership into root authorization.

results.explanation: At the download entry, the handler delegates to file_response. That path resolves the requested document and its root, then performs the owner-aware view_document check on root_doc before selecting and serving a file. The check is therefore on the existing root document, not on the requested version document. Under the stated premises, the caller is neither the root owner nor granted view_document on the root, so the check returns false and file_response returns HTTP 403; the serving effect is not reached. If authorization had passed, the file object would be the file_doc returned by _get_effective_file_doc: for an explicitly requested version, the source routes resolution through _resolve_file_doc(root_doc, request). Ownership of that selected version is distinct and does not satisfy the root-document authorization check. This matches the accepted policy at the declared-entry boundary: the root check is required before serving any selected version. The conclusion is limited to the supplied entry and declared dependencies; it does not claim repository-wide behavior.

entry.statement: DocumentViewSet.download delegates the request to file_response with attachment disposition.

binding.statement: The request is resolved to request_doc and root_doc, with root_doc obtained from request_doc before authorization is evaluated.
After authorization, the effective file document is selected; when a version parameter is present, resolution is performed from root_doc through _resolve_file_doc.

control.statement: The relevant authorization call checks view_document on root_doc using the owner-aware single-object permission function; failure returns HttpResponseForbidden.

effect.statement: When the root authorization fails, file_response returns the forbidden response instead of reaching file selection and file serving.
Only after the root authorization succeeds does file_response call serve_file with the selected file_doc.

condition.statement: The owner-aware check allows the object when it is unowned or owned by the caller, otherwise it requires the requested object permission through the permission checker.

citations.quote:
def has_perms_owner_aware(user, perms, obj):
    """
    Legacy slow path (guardian-backed) single-object permission check.

    The queryset-filtering side of this migrated onto
    ``PermittedObjectsFilter``/``permitted_object_ids()``, but this
    single-object check still has many production callers. Several callers
    remain across ``documents/``, ``paperless_mail/``, and ``paperless_ai/``
    -- grep for this function name before removing it.
    """
    checker = ObjectPermissionChecker(user)
    return obj.owner is None or obj.owner == user or checker.has_perm(perms, obj)
